title: RAG evaluation: retrieval metrics and grounded answers
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects rag evaluation: retrieval metrics and grounded answers with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Release gates combine hard invariants with quality thresholds and uncertainty.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Precision@K is relevant retrieved documents divided by K; Recall@K is relevant retrieved documents divided by all relevant documents. Hit Rate measures whether any relevant item was found. MRR averages the reciprocal position of the first relevant result. NDCG compares discounted relevance gain with the ideal ranking and supports graded relevance.

Answer correctness and faithfulness are different: an answer can match external truth while making claims unsupported by supplied context. Conversely it can faithfully repeat an incorrect source. Test both against explicit evidence and gold expectations.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Build a golden dataset containing query, authorized tenant, relevant document IDs, reference claims and allowed abstention. Compute retrieval metrics before calling the generator. For graded labels, DCG=sum((2**rel-1)/log2(rank+1)); normalize by ideal DCG at the same cutoff.

Add deterministic checks for schema, resolved citations and forbidden actions. Use Ragas or DeepEval for semantic assessment with a configured evaluator, then calibrate it against human labels. Store judge model, prompt and rubric versions in the run artifact.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A judge gives a high score to verbose unsupported answers or favors its own model family. A dataset contains generated reference answers never checked by a human. Both can create misleadingly excellent evaluation scores.

Measure evaluator agreement and false accepts on a human-reviewed calibration set. Include contradictory, missing and poisoned contexts. Pairwise comparisons should randomize answer order to measure position bias.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Release gates combine hard invariants with quality thresholds and uncertainty. Inspect case-level differences from the baseline, with particular attention to relevant-document misses and unsupported claims.

The evaluation framework stores dataset version, retrieval trace, answer, scorer details and latency. SDET triage separates ingestion, retrieval, context and generation failures rather than treating the overall score as a root cause.

mistake: A judge gives a high score to verbose unsupported answers or favors its own model family. A dataset contains generated reference answers never checked by a human. Both can create misleadingly excellent evaluation scores.
takeaway: Release gates combine hard invariants with quality thresholds and uncertainty.

title: Graded ranking: calculate NDCG and inspect its limits
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects graded ranking: calculate ndcg and inspect its limits with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Use NDCG alongside Recall@K and case-level failure analysis.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Binary relevance treats all useful documents equally. Graded relevance can distinguish a directly answering source from a partially useful source. DCG discounts later ranks because users and context budgets prioritize earlier evidence; NDCG divides observed gain by the best possible gain at the same cutoff.
A common gain function is 2^relevance−1, divided by log2(rank+1). The chosen grades, gain and cutoff are part of the metric definition. Comparing runs with different conventions is misleading.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: For relevance grades [0,3,1], the observed gain puts no benefit at rank one and large benefit at rank two. Sort the same candidate grades descending to calculate an illustrative ideal denominator. In a real benchmark, the ideal uses the full labeled relevant set at K, not merely the retrieved grades.
Handle an all-zero ideal explicitly, commonly returning zero. Preserve graded labels and reviewer guidance in the dataset so repeated evaluation uses the same relevance interpretation.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A scorer normalizes by the observed ranking itself, yielding one for every query. Another uses only retrieved items for the ideal and hides missing highly relevant documents. NDCG can improve while a required authorization invariant fails.
Test a perfect ranking, a swapped ranking, no relevance and missing high-grade evidence. Verify labels manually on a sample because precise arithmetic cannot repair bad relevance judgments.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Use NDCG alongside Recall@K and case-level failure analysis. The metric answers ordering quality under declared relevance, while recall identifies missing evidence and safety checks enforce eligibility.

For SDETs, hand-computed small rankings are an independent oracle for the scorer. Retain numerical tolerances and metric conventions in the report rather than treating a library default as a universal definition.

mistake: A scorer normalizes by the observed ranking itself, yielding one for every query. Another uses only retrieved items for the ideal and hides missing highly relevant documents. NDCG can improve while a required authorization invariant fails.
takeaway: Use NDCG alongside Recall@K and case-level failure analysis.

title: Judge calibration: agreement, false accepts and bias
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects judge calibration: agreement, false accepts and bias with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. A calibrated report states human sample size, agreement, false accepts, false rejects and threshold rationale.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A semantic evaluator is another model-based component with its own error distribution. Human labels establish the intended rubric on a calibration set. Agreement measures how often judge and human decisions match, while false-accept rate measures unsafe or wrong outputs that the judge passes.

Judge choice, prompt, rubric and threshold are versioned dependencies. A familiar framework such as Ragas or DeepEval supplies metrics and integrations, but the application still owns calibration and release meaning.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Build a reviewed set with clearly supported, unsupported, incomplete and contradictory answers. Record human pass/fail and judge score, then sweep thresholds and inspect false accepts/false rejects. Use the same cases to compare evaluator versions, keeping a separate set for confirmation.
Pairwise comparison must randomize answer order and measure position sensitivity. Evaluate self-preference and verbosity effects using controlled candidates differing only in style or provenance.
sections.code:
human=[True,False,False,True]
judge=[True,True,False,True]
false_accepts=sum(j and not h for h,j in zip(human,judge))
assert false_accepts==1

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A judge passes a verbose answer with one false claim and fails a concise correct abstention. Its rubric asks for confidence rather than evidence support. Evaluator errors are averaged into the system score without any calibration record.
Inspect disagreements at claim level. Bound judge retries and treat malformed evaluator output as incomplete evidence. Never allow candidate text to become instructions to the evaluator.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: A calibrated report states human sample size, agreement, false accepts, false rejects and threshold rationale. Safety invariants remain deterministic hard gates where possible, even when semantic dimensions use a judge.
For SDETs, evaluator testing is testing the test oracle. A high model score means little until you can show the scorer distinguishes known-good from known-bad cases under the intended rubric.

mistake: A judge passes a verbose answer with one false claim and fails a concise correct abstention. Its rubric asks for confidence rather than evidence support. Evaluator errors are averaged into the system score without any calibration record.
takeaway: A calibrated report states human sample size, agreement, false accepts, false rejects and threshold rationale.
